title: Canonical comparisons for pairwise overlap base change
statement: For a contravariant Cat-valued pseudofunctor on a category with pullbacks, the canonical base change of a universal pair map is its pullHom along the induced overlap map, conjugated by the two composition comparisons. The pair square asserts that this map commutes with specified component isomorphisms and a descent datum [def-pc-local-overlap-transitions]. For scheme modules on an iterated open-cover pullback [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-base-change], construct the chart map to the direct limit chart by pullback.lift and construct its component comparison by pullback composition, equality-of-arrow isomorphisms, and pullback of the specified direct comparison. The specialized overlapPairSquare uses this generic pair square. These are exactly the five pre-existing constructions relocated without mathematical change. The existing public limit/stage composition lemma stays in the original pair-map module.

source.place: First proof, canonical successive restriction comparisons

proof.text: The five definitions use universal pullback maps, pullHom, the pseudofunctor composition comparisons and the given component isomorphisms; none chooses an existence witness. Their construction bodies are unchanged. The composition lemma remains in its original module.

lean.statement:
def overlapPairBaseChangeHom
    {C : Type (u + 1)} [Category.{u} C] [HasPullbacks C]
    (F : Pseudofunctor (LocallyDiscrete Cᵒᵖ) Cat.{u, u + 1})
    {S X₁ X₂ S' X₁' X₂' : C} (f₁ : X₁ ⟶ S) (f₂ : X₂ ⟶ S)
    (p : S' ⟶ S) (p₁ : X₁' ⟶ X₁) (p₂ : X₂' ⟶ X₂)
    (f₁' : X₁' ⟶ S') (f₂' : X₂' ⟶ S')
    (w₁ : p₁ ≫ f₁ = f₁' ≫ p) (w₂ : p₂ ≫ f₂ = f₂' ≫ p)
    (N₁ : F.obj (.mk (op X₁))) (N₂ : F.obj (.mk (op X₂)))
    (φ : (F.map (pullback.fst f₁ f₂).op.toLoc).toFunctor.obj N₁ ⟶
      (F.map (pullback.snd f₁ f₂).op.toLoc).toFunctor.obj N₂) :
    (F.map (pullback.fst f₁' f₂').op.toLoc).toFunctor.obj
        ((F.map p₁.op.toLoc).toFunctor.obj N₁) ⟶
      (F.map (pullback.snd f₁' f₂').op.toLoc).toFunctor.obj
        ((F.map p₂.op.toLoc).toFunctor.obj N₂)
